newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB to be first western bank in Murmansk.
newsitem.headline: DnB to be first western bank in Murmansk.

text.p: Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's largest bank, said on Thursday it will apply to Russian and Norwegian authorities for a concession to set up a subsidiary in Murmansk on the Kola peninsula.

"DnB will be the first foreign-owned bank in North-West Russia," a statement said. "The European Bank of Research and Development (ERBD) will be invited to participate with a minority stake, while DnB will be in charge of operations in DnB Murmansk."

Together with DnB in Norway, DnB in Murmansk will offer bank services to Norwegian and Russian companies, as well as companies with headquarters in other countries in connection with the growing business activity in North West Russia, it said.
Dnb said it would open a representative office in Murmansk, which is situated near the Norwegian border, by the end of this year pending approval of the application to establish the subisidary.
Trade between Russia and Norway has almost doubled over the past four years, amounting to 5.4 billion crowns last year, DnB said.
Trade between North-West Russia and Northern Norway has shown particularly strong growth and Norway is now the Murmansk area's major international trading partner, the statement said.
"The area is rich in natural resources and has considerable potential for business development within oil and gas, minerals, fishing and forestry," the bank said.
